candidate.answerReason: Substituting the given root and equating imaginary and real parts gives r=-12 and s=26.

methods.label: Substitute the root and compare parts
methods.explanation:
Because \(3+2i\) is a root, substituting it makes the polynomial zero. This gives an equality whose real and imaginary parts must each be zero. Using \(i^2=-1\), first calculate
\[
(3+2i)^2=9+12i+4i^2=5+12i.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
0&=2(5+12i)+r(3+2i)+s\\
&=(10+3r+s)+(24+2r)i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(r\) and \(s\) are real, the imaginary part gives \(24+2r=0\), so \(r=-12\). The real part then gives
\[
10+3(-12)+s=0,
\]
so \(s=26\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Complex multiplication and comparison of real and imaginary parts are directly appropriate to the given complex root; the remaining equations are linear.
